title: Operational service contract and failure-mode matrix for model endpoints
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines an operational "service contract" for model endpoints that ties concrete SLIs to automated error-budget actions: circuit breakers, load-shedding rules, and multi-region failover triggers. The goal is to give product teams a predictable reliability model per endpoint/model variant while enabling automated, measurable graceful degradation to preserve core user experience and to protect regional capacity during incidents.

Scope:
- Formal SLI definitions (availability, latency P95/P99, model-quality regression SLI) measured per endpoint+model-variant and aggregated by customer tier.
- Error budget accounting and burn-rate thresholds for soft/hard remediation.
- Circuit breaker states, thresholds, and cooldown behavior (per-route and per-customer).
- Load-shedding policies (priority hierarchy, batching/backfill rules, token caps, streaming degradation).
- Multi-region failover policy, health signals, and failback criteria.
- Example failure-mode matrix for common incident types with playbook mapping.

Why this is needed:
We frequently deploy new model variants and routing rules; teams need a single, auditable contract that maps measured reliability signals to deterministic, automated actions. Current scatter of SLI definitions causes inconsistent failover behaviors and customer confusion during incidents. This work reduces toil, improves multi-region resilience, and ensures predictable error-budget enforcement across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

High-level decisions so far:
- SLIs will be defined at endpoint+model-version granularity. Aggregation tiers available: per-route, per-customer, per-region, and global.
- Primary SLIs: availability (success-rate), latency (p95 and p99 of server-side processing excluding network), and model-quality (percent of evaluation prompts passing threshold).
- Error budget is expressed as fractional failures over a 30d rolling window for availability/latency, and as regression percentage for model-quality.
- Two-tiered remediation: soft (automated routing adjustments + throttling) and hard (circuit-breaker open -> degrade to fallback model or region failover).

Measurement details (examples):
- Availability SLI: fraction of requests returning 2xx with valid model output within deadline. Measure window: 30d rolling and 5m for burn-rate detection.
- Latency SLI: p95/p99 of server processing time (start of handler to final token produced). Target example: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 1200ms for low-latency tier.
- Model-quality SLI: % of a sampled production prompt-set that passes acceptance checks (semantic match / hallucination threshold). Evaluate hourly on a reservoir-sampled set of 1k prompts per model.
- Cardinality: compute SLIs per (route, model_variant, region, customer_tier). Aggregations apply weighted averaging where weight = request count / tokens to reflect economic impact.

Error budget math (example):
- Goal: 99.9% availability over 30d. Budget = 0.1% of requests. If baseline is 10M requests/day, monthly budget ~30M * 0.001 = 30k requests.
- Burn rate calculation window: 1h and 6h short-term windows to detect incidents. Burn rate = observed failures / expected allowed failures in window. If burn_rate > 2 for 1h -> soft remediation; burn_rate > 8 for 1h -> hard remediation. Values adjustable per tier.

Circuit breaker design notes:
- CB is scoped at three levels: route, model-variant, and customer. Each level maintains independent state with hierarchical precedence (customer > route > model).
- States: CLOSED, RECOVERING (half-open probe traffic), OPEN.
- Metrics to trigger OPEN: consecutive failure ratio above threshold (e.g., 10% failure over 1m and burn_rate > 4), p99 latency spike (relative increase > 5x baseline), or sustained model-quality regression > 3%.
- Cooldown: exponential backoff for auto-retry; base timeout 60s, doubling up to 1h. During OPEN, low-priority/background requests are immediately rejected; critical requests are routed to fallback model/region.

Load-shedding policy (priority-driven):
- Priority buckets: critical (user-facing realtime), interactive (chat UI), bulk-batch (embeddings/long-running), background (async analytics).
- When capacity constrained: 1) refuse background tasks, 2) throttle batch concurrency, 3) reduce max tokens for interactive, 4) switch streaming to batched non-streaming.
- Token-budget per-tenant: implement soft token-rate caps that degrade to hard caps when customer error budget is exhausted.

Multi-region failover:
- Active-active preferred for low-latency tiers. Traffic steering should be weighted by region health signals (RUM + server-side p95/p99 + region error-rate).
- Failover triggers: sustained region-level SLI breach (region p99 > 2x global baseline OR region availability < 98% for 10m) and region error budget burn_rate > 3.
- Failback: only after region SLIs return to within 80% of baseline for a 30m observation window and error budget burn rate < 1.2 for 1h.
- Data considerations: KV cache warmup and KV cache sync policy when failing over (prefer cache-less fallbacks for safety; gradual ramp-up to avoid cache stampede).

Failure-mode matrix (example rows):
- Model crash (OOM): CB opens at model-variant level; route directs to smaller-quantized variant; notify on-call; create rollback if burn persists.
- GPU saturation regionally: soft-shed batch, throttle new requests, start failover to secondary region for critical traffic.
- Model quality regression (A/B): if model-quality SLI drops > 2% relative to baseline AND error budget usage high -> immediate rollback to previous model, mark variant as quarantined.
- Networking partition: route-level CBs open for affected region, redirect to other regions if user session supports cross-region failover.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clear SLI definitions documented and approved by reliability and product teams.
- Error budget math and burn-rate thresholds set for three customer tiers and codified in policy table.
- Circuit breaker state machine implemented with configurable thresholds and cooldowns in runtime config.
- Load-shedding rules implemented in routing layer with a priority bucket evaluator.
- Multi-region failover test plan and one successful dry-run failover executed in staging.
